chunks: But (to) those who were victimised and left their homes and then fought and endured patiently, your Lord will surely be forgiving and kind.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who emigrate and strive patiently after persecution?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Ahl al-Bayt and their companions who endured persecution before the Great Migration (Hijrah) or during the early Islamic period, highlighting the transition from passive suffering to active striving (Jihad). It underscores the divine promise that after enduring trials (Fitnah) and maintaining patience (Sabr), God’s mercy becomes the ultimate recompense for the steadfast. This reinforces the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and political resilience of the Imams and their followers in the face of oppression.
